correspondence.component_scope: Chosen eastern opening and north-northwest upper-valley approach
correspondence.finding: The original map shows a small upper channel in the chosen eastern valley continuing north-northwest through its tributary joins toward the northern bend of the named Inglutalik corridor. The selected beginning lies in this mapped feeder setting. Ordinary valley and through-channel correspondence is visible without requiring a separate name for the small opening reach.
correspondence.name_scope: Connected upper feeder; no separate feeder name assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern upper bend and southwestward turn
correspondence.finding: The mapped upper channel turns west across the northern bend and then southwest into the valley explicitly labeled Inglutalik River. The entering feeder, intervening joins and outgoing reach occupy the same ordinary connected corridor as the supplied selection.
correspondence.name_scope: Named Inglutalik River upper corridor, with no exact formal name-start vertex assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Westward middle valley and intervening bends and joins
correspondence.finding: The source depicts a continuous meandering river across the selected middle valley. Northern and southern side streams enter this trunk while the selected route remains on its westward corridor. The named upper and lower portions are linked by the visible river rather than by basin membership alone.

correspondence.component_scope: Southwestern valley descent and transition to the lower plain
correspondence.finding: The mapped river turns southwest through the widening valley, receives the visible side-stream junctions and continues into the southward lower-valley reach. Its meanders and changes in valley direction establish the ordinary through-link represented by these selected parts.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward lower river and approach to the delta turn
correspondence.finding: Repeated Inglutalik River labels follow the large meandering channel south through the lowland. The selected route stays within this continuous lower-river corridor and reaches its westward delta approach. Nearby ponds and side drainage do not substitute for the mapped trunk.

The original shows the lower river turning west and continuing through the broad delta channel, with Inglutalik River labels within the delta itself. This passage remains distinguishable from the surrounding ponds and secondary channels and connects the lower valley to the selected coastal outlet at ordinary regional scale.
correspondence.name_scope: Inglutalik River delta corridor; no unique name or current flow allocation is assigned to each branch.

correspondence.finding: The selected final segment occupies the mapped outlet where the Inglutalik delta channel opens into coastal water. The source establishes the outgoing mouth and adjacent shoreline setting, rather than merely locating a terminal inside the same drainage basin.
correspondence.name_scope: Mouth of the representative Inglutalik River system; coastal water is not assigned a river scalar name.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen headward opening and first upper reach
correspondence.finding: The supplied selected line starts with a short northward opening and then turns west. This is model orientation only.
The selected upper corridor continues west through several stored pieces. No original map or authorial passage was available to establish its physical through-links.
The supplied path bends north and northwest. No independent source establishes this chosen middle corridor or its tributary joins.
The selected line turns farther west before the coastal approach. Bluegoose is a discovery lead for the region, not a mapped identification of these pieces.

correspondence.component_scope: Final coastal approach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: The supplied model marks a sea terminal. Its actual receiving waterbody and the selected final channel have not been independently established.

The chosen opening is in the mountainous drainage west of Mundo Nuevo, near the La Piedra–Cerro Pucara setting. The original chart depicts several adjacent headward valleys and their southern plain outlets. It does not unambiguously establish the selected initial feeder through all of its southward and westward turns into the Oregano corridor. No upstream Neverí or Turimiquire-reservoir name is assigned to this opening.

The chart directly labels Río Oregano in the plain southeast of Santa Inés and depicts its tributary network and southern bends around the Portrerito oilfield area. These are positive regional anchors for the selected eastern and southern corridor. Generalized and partly overprinted small-channel linework does not resolve every selected through-link around the southern return; the Oregano label is not extended over every feeder.

The selected westward lowland reach and its turn near La Chorrera correspond at ordinary corridor scale to the charted Río Aragua, north of Portrerito. The nearby Río Prespuntual enters from the south and is a distinct tributary, rather than an alternative name for the selected opening.

The chart depicts the northward Aragua corridor from La Chorrera and the Querecual approach near Sabaneta/Querecual. The hydrology chapter independently identifies Querecual and Prespuntual as Aragua tributaries. These support the intermediate network and distinguish it from the Neverí headwater valley farther north.

The selection continues northwest and north through the La Boqueita–Barcelona approach. The historical chart supplies a lower channel-network setting, but its regional linework and infrastructure overprinting do not settle the selected through-link. Córdova Rodríguez and González Sanabria state that Aragua was diverted in 1970 toward the Chivacoa plain and the sea west of Barcelona airport, while Capiricual and Naricual remain with Neverí. The relationship of the selected northward connector to the diverted Aragua route, its former connection and the lower Neverí therefore remains material pending. This is a missing geographic/managed-connection explanation, not a demand for present discharge, exact banks or operational verification.

The actual selected ending is the Barcelona coastal outlet setting on the Caribbean, rather than the separately described Aragua outlet west of the airport. The chart depicts the city/coastal channel network and the hydrology chapter states that Neverí reaches the Caribbean through Barcelona. These support the bounded lower Neverí/sea-terminal identity; they do not prove the unresolved upstream Aragua transfer. No offshore extension or alternate Aragua mouth is substituted for the selected ending.

The pinned selection starts at its western end and continues eastward through the first three stored parts. No source map or imagery was read for this opening, and no named headwater, ice body, lake, or through-connection can be assigned from the coastal prose.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper eastward continuation and shallow southern bend
correspondence.finding: The upper stored continuation turns slightly south before resuming northeastward. Its intervening joins lack independent terrain or hydrographic correspondence. The model's line is orientation only; neither glacier passage nor an ordinary open-channel reach is established.

The long middle route and all its stored joins remain without inspected cartographic coverage. Potential lakes, glacial passages, valley transfers and tributary junctions are not identified. No hydraulic or natural-river identity is inferred from the modeled connection.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeastward approach to the northern bend
correspondence.finding: The selected northeastward progression toward its northernmost bend has not been associated with an independently depicted watercourse or terrain corridor. Coastal descriptions do not supply these inland through-links.

The northernmost selected turn and subsequent southeastward continuation remain uncorroborated. ARC402 names Murray Lake as draining toward Simmons Bay, but supplies no inland map proving that this selected bend crosses that lake or its outlet. Murray Lake is retained only as a contextual clue.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower southeastward approach and actual terminal
correspondence.finding: ARC402 identifies Simmons Bay on the north shore of Archer Fiord, opposite Bulleys Lump, and describes a river from Murray Lake reaching the bay's head through a steep canyon. This is a useful broad contextual match for the selected coastal vicinity. Without a map of the selected final approach and outlet, it does not prove which channel or bay-head location is the actual selected terminal, or establish the connection to the full inland selection.
